notes.title: Operating philosophy
notes.body: This is a coaching first org. Leaders spend their time coaching: team meetings, 1:1s, reviewing calls and emails, and giving real time feedback. Managers and directors must have serious hands on SDR experience, know how to coach, and have been coached themselves. We deliberately avoid an org bogged down in tools training and low value meetings.

notes.title: Span of control
notes.body: One manager per 8 SDRs, not 10, to leave real room for coaching. One director per roughly 50 SDRs. At roughly 233 SDRs that lands at about 29 managers and 5 directors.

notes.title: Messaging is owned by Product Marketing
notes.body: Product Marketing already provides messaging and content, so messaging is owned by PMM and not by this org. Enablement operationalizes what PMM produces into rep ready sequences and talk tracks.

notes.title: Enablement stays lean
notes.body: Enablement is deliberately a single role, scoped so it does not duplicate Product Marketing or the managers. It is measured on ramp to productivity, not on the number of training sessions run.

notes.title: Existing shared functions
notes.body: Rev Ops, Sales Recruiter and Talent Partner, and Content and Messaging already exist on the current team. They support this org on a dotted line and are not net new hires here.

roleDefinitions.title: Head of Inside Sales (VP)
responsibilities: Owns the entire SDR org, its number of 7,000 completed demos per quarter, and the operating model.
Builds and leads the leadership layer, sets the coaching culture, and hires and develops the directors.
Owns capacity planning, headcount ramp, targets, comp, and reporting to the COO.
Stays close to the floor and protects the org from meeting and tool bloat.

roleDefinitions.title: Director of SDR
responsibilities: Owns a segment of about 50 SDRs across roughly 6 managers, and their share of the demo target.
Develops and coaches the managers, the coach the coach work, runs manager 1:1s, and holds the coaching standard.
Accountable for team demo output, ramp, and quality, and removes blockers.
Must have real SDR and people management experience.

roleDefinitions.title: SDR Manager / Team Lead
responsibilities: Owns a team of 8 SDRs and their demo number.
Spends the majority of time coaching: team meetings, weekly 1:1s, reviewing calls and emails, and real time feedback.
Hires, ramps, develops, and manages the performance of the team, and runs the pod cadence.
Must have serious hands on SDR experience, know how to coach, and have been coached.

roleDefinitions.title: SDR
responsibilities: Owns 13 scheduled and 10 completed demos per month against target accounts.
Runs outbound across calls, email, and social, books and holds qualified demos, and hands off cleanly to AEs.
Executes the plays and messaging, which come from Product Marketing and are operationalized by Enablement, and acts on coaching.
Keeps CRM and activity data clean.

roleDefinitions.title: SDR Enablement Lead
responsibilities: Owns new hire onboarding and ramp certification across the first 30, 60 and 90 days, and is accountable for ramp to productivity time.
Builds the coaching infrastructure, call scoring rubrics, playbooks, and 1:1 and call review frameworks, and trains the managers to coach.
Owns the SDR tool stack, dialer, sequencer and conversation intelligence, and keeps training lightweight and just in time.
Operationalizes Product Marketing messaging into rep ready sequences, talk tracks, and objection handling.
Deliberately lean, measured on ramp rather than on session count.

roleDefinitions.title: Rev / Sales Ops
responsibilities: Reporting, tooling, data, and comp and quota mechanics.

roleDefinitions.title: Sales Recruiter / Talent
responsibilities: Fills the hiring pipeline at wave velocity.

roleDefinitions.title: Product Marketing
responsibilities: Owns messaging, positioning, and content.
